---
title: "Research"
description: "Papers, preprints, thesis, dissertation, software and research projects on graphical models, stochastic processes and spatial statistics."
---

My research focuses on **inference for stochastic processes** and **model selection**, mainly for graphical models (Markov random fields) under mixing conditions. I have also worked on Bayesian spatial statistics, multivariate time series and change-point detection.

[Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com.br/citations?user=Isftae0AAAAJ){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm} [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3432-7779){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm} [Lattes](https://lattes.cnpq.br/9791024128849349){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm} [GitHub](https://github.com/magnotairone){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}

## Software

-   [**MixingGraph**](https://github.com/magnotairone/MixingGraph) (R package): implements the estimator, proposed in the thesis, of the conditional dependence graph of random vectors under a mixing condition, with four algorithms to compute the estimated graph.
-   [**GeoJAGS**](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geojags/files/) (C++ module for JAGS): Bayesian hierarchical models for georeferenced data, with 11 covariance functions for point-referenced data (including Matérn) and the conditional autoregressive (CAR) model for areal data.

## Research projects

-   **Graphical models under mixing conditions** (IME-USP, 2018–2024): a global penalized model selection criterion to estimate the conditional dependence graph of a multivariate stochastic process, with no need to estimate and combine the neighborhoods of each vertex. We proved strong consistency of the estimator under a mixing condition, chose the penalty by cross-validation, and applied the method to São Francisco River flow measurements and to daily stock market indices. It led to the thesis, the *Stochastic Processes and their Applications* paper and the MixingGraph package.
-   **Independent blocks in multivariate time series** (joint project between USP and the University of Buenos Aires, during the PhD): a criterion to find independence points in vector-valued stochastic processes and split the vector into independent blocks. It led to the *Journal of Time Series Analysis* paper.
-   **Change-point detection in the COVID-19 curve** (GPECA, IME-USP, 2020): splines and model selection to track the trend of new cases in Brazil, its states and cities, and other countries, with a [daily updated page](https://www.ime.usp.br/~gpeca/covid-19/covid-19.html) from April to December 2020.
-   **Extending JAGS for spatial data** (DEST-UFMG, 2016–2018): led to the dissertation and to GeoJAGS.

-   Review of the Portuguese translation of [R for Data Science (2nd edition)](https://pt.r4ds.hadley.nz/) (2023–2024).
